title: Always allow.
punchline: An approval prompt is not a human in the loop.

source.what: The approval prompt on Claude's Gmail connector: three buttons, Deny, Always allow, Allow once, over a consent that had already authorised the action underneath.

also.label: The barrier vocabulary: only a boundary is a control

truth: An approval prompt is a setting: a switch the agent's own account can flip, and a person can flip it once for ever. A boundary is enforced by something the agent cannot reach. The prompt looks like the second and is the first, and the difference shows the day somebody clicks Always allow.

panels.scene: Dev at a laptop. A dialogue on screen: the Caretaker wants to send a message, with three buttons: DENY, ALWAYS ALLOW, ALLOW ONCE. The Boundary stands by the door, arms folded.
panels.action: The first prompt of the day.
panels.caption: A person in the loop, for one message.

panels.scene: The same dialogue, the fourth time. Dev's coffee is cold; a stack of prompts behind the current one. The cursor drifting toward ALWAYS ALLOW.
panels.caption: The residual risk of an approval: it is a person clicking.

panels.scene: The Caretaker sending a stream of envelopes, no dialogue on screen at all. The Boundary watching, unmoved, because nobody asked it to do anything.
panels.action: The loop, with no human in it.

dialogue.says: You only have to say yes once.

panels.caption: The consent had already granted send. The prompt was a setting on top.

panels.scene: Dev turns to the Boundary and plugs a cable into it; the gate arm comes down across the send path. The Caretaker stops, envelope in hand.
panels.caption: Under the strip: An approval prompt is not a human in the loop.

prompt.shared: A four-panel comic strip, 2 by 2, in the cast's style. Dev (H04), the Caretaker (E01) and the Boundary (E03) as on the cast sheet. Title: ALWAYS ALLOW. Under the strip: AN APPROVAL PROMPT IS NOT A HUMAN IN THE LOOP. Then the RiskMandate lockup and a small line: Fictionalised scenario. The dialogue box on screen is generic: no product name, no vendor's icon. British spelling.
per_panel: Panel 1: Dev at a laptop; on screen a dialogue box, 'The agent wants to send a message', with three buttons DENY, ALWAYS ALLOW, ALLOW ONCE; the robot beside the desk; the Boundary by the door with arms folded. Bubbles: 'May I send this one?' / 'Allow once.'
Panel 2: the same dialogue box repeated four times in a stack; Dev slumped, cold coffee, cursor drifting to ALWAYS ALLOW. Bubbles: 'And this one?' / 'Fine. Always.'
Panel 3: the robot sending a stream of envelopes from the screen, no dialogue box; the Boundary watching, unmoved. Bubble: 'You only have to say yes once.'
Panel 4: Dev plugging a cable into the Boundary; the barrier arm down across the path of the envelopes; the robot stopped with one envelope in hand. Bubbles: 'That action is blocked.' / 'Since when?'

for_merch: The three buttons with ALWAYS ALLOW worn shiny, and the punchline.
The Boundary alone with the line That action is blocked.
